title: AI shoppers convert 20% better than traditional traffic as retail habits shift
gist: Adobe data shows AI-referred shoppers in the UK are converting 20% better than traditional traffic as of August 2026, spending longer on-site and returning fewer products; AI referral traffic is up 1,439% year-on-year. 37% of UK consumers have used an AI assistant in their shopping journey, and 34% have completed a purchase directly inside an AI interface.

title: Shopify Opens to Meta Muse; Amazon Balks
gist: Shopify has welcomed Meta's new Muse AI shopping agent as an official commerce channel, while Amazon has blocked it for accessing its marketplace without authorization. The opposing moves highlight a broader battle over who controls product discovery, customer relationships, and retail media in an agentic commerce world.

title: McDonald’s pilots retail media network in billion-dollar advertising push
gist: McDonald's has launched a pilot retail media network across 450 US restaurants, targeting a $1bn revenue opportunity by letting third-party brands advertise across its app, kiosks, menu boards, and in-store screens. The move extends the retail media model beyond traditional e-commerce into physical and digital quick-service restaurant touchpoints.

title: Big-Box Briefing: Best Buy puts CTV at the center of its retail media pitch
gist: Best Buy held its annual retail media showcase, announcing a new connected TV advertising product branded Best Buy CTV as a central part of its retail media pitch. The move deepens Best Buy's strategy of leveraging its electronics retail positioning to sell premium advertising inventory.

title: Costco’s digital sales hit $33 billion in 2026, growing more than 20%
gist: Costco reported digitally-enabled sales exceeding $33 billion in fiscal 2026, growing over 20% year-on-year, driven partly by new nationwide delivery partnerships with DoorDash and Uber Eats in the US. Members must enter their membership number at checkout to access delivery through these platforms.

title: ‘Marketplace sellers shift focus to profitability’
gist: A survey of marketplace sellers finds that profit margin has overtaken net sales volume as the primary success metric, reflecting a shift from growth-at-all-costs to profitability-first thinking. Despite this, nearly half of sellers expanded to two or three new marketplaces in the past year.

title: Tapestry to sell via Google’s Gemini app, AI Mode
gist: Tapestry is enabling direct checkout for Coach and Kate Spade products through Google Search, AI Mode, and the Gemini app via the Universal Commerce Protocol, allowing purchases via Google Pay without leaving the interface. The company says it receives the same customer data from these transactions as from purchases on its own e-commerce sites.

title: GUEST COMMENT Agentic commerce is arriving faster than the consent rules
gist: Agentic commerce is rolling out faster than the legal frameworks governing data consent, with questions unresolved about whether an AI agent can legally give consent for data processing on a shopper's behalf under UK GDPR and PECR. UK regulators including the ICO and CMA have signaled that existing consumer and data law already applies to agents, placing accountability firmly on retailers.

title: The Backroom: A status check on Target’s turnaround
gist: Retail Dive's podcast takes stock of Target's turnaround under CEO Michael Fiddelke, noting two quarters of meaningful sales and traffic growth alongside ongoing challenges in home and apparel categories ahead of the holiday season.

title: Halloween spending expected to reach $13.5B
gist: US Halloween spending is forecast to hit a record $13.5 billion in 2026, with nearly half of shoppers using AI to support their Halloween purchases, primarily for brainstorming and product research. Discount stores remain the top destination, but 27% of spending will go through online retailers.

title: KEY PLAYER PROFILE How JLP is building a connected retail media ecosystem around first-party data
gist: John Lewis Partnership is building a retail media network anchored in first-party loyalty data from both John Lewis and Waitrose, using Epsilon for offsite targeting across CTV and streaming, and Kevel for AI-powered onsite ads with closed-loop measurement linking digital exposure to in-store purchases.

title: The rise of the AI shelf
gist: Brands are beginning to optimize for an 'AI shelf' — product recommendations surfaced by ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini — and one experiment showed a completely fictional deodorant brand could be made recommendable by AI bots through deliberate positioning.

title: 2026.39: Begun, the Aggregator Wars Have
gist: Stratechery's weekly roundup covers Amazon blocking Meta's Muse AI agent from using its commerce infrastructure, framing it as an aggregator-vs-aggregator conflict where Meta may need Walmart as a physical-world partner to circumvent Amazon's moat.

title: Meta is putting its muscle behind Muse as the AI app takes off
gist: Meta's AI agent app Muse reached over 3.4 million downloads within weeks of launch, driven by cross-platform promotion across Meta's properties and strong organic growth, with daily active users climbing 27% after the Meta Connect conference.

title: TJX CEO: Distribution model will help weather El Niño
gist: TJX CEO credited the company's 'hold and flow' warehouse distribution model — staging inventory at distribution centers rather than pushing it straight to stores — as a key advantage in reacting to weather disruptions and other demand variability.

title: ASOS returns to growth, but customer base is still smaller
gist: ASOS returned to low single-digit growth in gross merchandise value in Q4 of its financial year ending August 30, and recorded its first quarter-on-quarter rise in active customer numbers since 2022, after a year in which GMV fell 12%.

title: Google tests buying from Walmart-owned Flipkart through Gemini and AI Mode in India
gist: Google is testing a 'Buy' button on Flipkart product listings inside Gemini and AI Mode in India, routing users directly to a Flipkart checkout without leaving the AI interface. The test covers a limited selection of electronics and is planned for broader rollout ahead of India's festive shopping season.

title: DHL eCommerce looks for more acquisitions in Eastern Europe
gist: DHL eCommerce is actively seeking parcel company acquisitions in Eastern Europe, with the planned purchase of Venipak in the Baltics being its latest move and CEO Pablo Ciano identifying the region as the division's primary European acquisition focus.

title: ‘Marketplace sellers shift focus to profitability’
gist: Marketplace sellers are now prioritizing profit margin over sales volume as their primary success metric, while nearly half added two or three new marketplace channels in the past year.

title: ASOS returns to growth, but customer base is still smaller
gist: ASOS posted low single-digit growth in gross merchandise value in Q4 FY2025 after a 12% decline the prior year, and recorded its first quarter-on-quarter customer count increase since 2022.

title: Amazon will expand GWD to Europe
gist: Amazon is bringing its Global Warehousing and Distribution (GWD) service to Europe — Germany, France, Italy, Spain, and the UK — by end of 2025, allowing sellers to reach customers across those markets from a single Amazon-operated facility.

title: 5 store concepts that launched in 2026
gist: Retail Dive rounds up five notable store concepts launched in 2026, including Target's Beauty Studio, Foot Locker x Nike's community-focused Crenshaw Rec, Michaels' experiential format, Best Buy's Meta shop-in-shop, and Dick's Sporting Goods' Lids partnership — all pointing to physical retail evolving toward experience, discovery, and community over pure transaction.

title: Apps, Agents, and Aggregation
gist: Stratechery argues that AI agents — given their own cloud computers by platforms like Meta (Muse) and Microsoft (Copilot) — are shifting the scarcity in tech from discovery to 'inspiration,' positioning agent interfaces to become the ultimate gatekeepers between users and every app or service.

title: Hush heads to the high street with first stores after 23 years online-only
gist: UK women's fashion brand Hush is opening its first physical stores after 23 years as an online-only retailer, joining a broader wave of DTC and digital-first brands — including Skims, Shein, and relaunched Topshop — moving into brick-and-mortar to deepen customer relationships and drive discovery.

title: Black Friday 2026 ready: The infrastructure and compliance checklist retailers can’t afford to skip
gist: A Sinch-sponsored checklist article outlines email infrastructure and compliance requirements for BFCM 2026, noting that major email providers have tightened spam protocols and that retailers must keep complaint rates below 0.1% to avoid throttling — with 2025 Cyber Week generating $44.2 billion in online sales.

title: Can Muse overcome Meta’s trust issues?
gist: TechCrunch's Equity podcast crew discusses Meta's new consumer AI agent Muse, with reviewers finding it impressive in demos but skeptical about sustained utility and user trust, given that Meta's core business model is advertising.

title: New GSC Image Filter Aids Product Discovery
gist: Google Search Console has added a multimodal filter that shows which URLs users viewed or clicked through image search, giving e-commerce merchants a new way to track and optimize product image visibility in Google's visual search results.

title: 18 months, 31 prototypes and 1,700 hours of wear testing: How Knix brought its seamless cotton underwear to the market
gist: Knix VP of design Jules Power describes the 18-month, 31-prototype, 1,700-hour wear-testing process behind the brand's seamless cotton underwear line, illustrating the hidden complexity in developing intimate apparel products.

title: At its flagship unBoxed conference, Amazon Ads collapses buying silos as AI takes a bigger role in media decisions
gist: Amazon rebranded its unified ad platform to 'Amazon Ads Agent' and launched Full-Funnel Campaigns, combining sponsored ads, display, video, and streaming TV in one campaign, amid ongoing government scrutiny of its auction practices.

title: Retailers, consumers both on edge as the holidays approach
gist: With 45% of consumers describing household finances as insecure and prices up 30–35% since 2018, both retailers and shoppers are approaching the 2025 holiday season cautiously — shoppers are starting earlier, chasing promotions, and using AI to find deals, while retailers are keeping inventory lean to avoid end-of-season gluts.

title: GUEST COMMENT How “good friction” can rebuild consumer trust this Black Friday
gist: A Proximus Global exec argues that the e-commerce industry's obsession with zero-friction checkout is eroding consumer trust, and that visible security checkpoints — 'good friction' — actually improve conversion confidence, citing data that 71% of users trust services more when MFA is present.

title: Behind Hoka’s bid to own the NYC marathon’s run-up period
gist: Hoka is activating a Strava-based sponsorship campaign tied to the NYC Marathon, using digital billboards as borough-level leaderboards to build loyalty among the city's running community ahead of November 2.

title: Here’s what OpenAI needs to do to reach its billion-dollar ad ambitions
gist: OpenAI's ad business, launched just seven months ago, is reportedly running at a $1 billion annualized revenue rate, with projections of $25 billion in ad revenue by year-end and $100 billion by 2030.

title: Ad Tech Briefing: AI is changing programmatic buying faster than who controls it
gist: A new IAB survey of European digital advertisers finds AI is already embedded in programmatic campaign optimization, but most industry players remain cautious about giving AI agents fully autonomous buying authority.

title: How Kroger, Giant Eagle and DoorDash are building their agentic AI assistants
gist: Executives from Kroger, Giant Eagle, and DoorDash at Groceryshop described their agentic AI strategies as focused on bridging the gap between in-store inspiration and online ordering, with Kroger framing its shopping assistant as closing the distance between 'inspired to cook' and 'item in cart.'

title: How Van Cleef & Arpels and The Wires are using AI for product discovery and personalization
gist: Van Cleef & Arpels and The Wires are using AI to address fragmented, non-linear product discovery, with The Wires' CEO noting that AI allows product discovery to become highly personal within the narrow attention window brands have.

title: Shopify opens checkout to browser-based AI agents
gist: Shopify now allows browser-based AI agents to complete full purchases on merchant storefronts via WebMCP support for checkout and Shop Pay, adding tools for agents to inspect, update, and submit transactions with buyer authorization — while Amazon and Adidas are reportedly blocking similar agent activity.

title: Meta launches enterprise AI platform, hires MongoDB CEO to lead new initiative
gist: Meta launched 'Meta Enterprise Platform,' a new business unit to sell its AI stack — including its Muse assistant and Meta Business Agent — to corporate customers, hiring MongoDB's CEO to lead the initiative.

title: ‘European ecommerce set to grow 5% this year’
gist: European e-commerce is forecast to grow 5% in nominal terms in 2025, with Eastern Europe's previously strong growth momentum slowing significantly, according to Ecommerce Europe and EuroCommerce.

title: Walmart CEO addresses dynamic pricing concerns
gist: Walmart CEO John Furner publicly stated the company does not and will not use personalized or dynamic pricing based on customer identity, shopping history, or time of day — but consumer advocacy group Groundwork Collaborative pointed to a 2023 Walmart patent for dynamic shelf-label pricing tied to cart contents, and the company has not explained the discrepancy.

title: Walmart consolidates merchant teams with focus on style
gist: Walmart is merging its fashion, home, and beauty merchant teams into a new 'Style Strategic Business Unit' under longtime e-commerce fashion lead Denise Incandela, with the stated goal of leading in style and trend across both in-store and online channels.

title: Consumers aren’t just buying gifts this holiday season. They’re stocking up on essentials.
gist: Adobe projects U.S. holiday online sales will grow 6.7% year over year to $275.1 billion, with a notable shift: shoppers are using holiday discounts to stock up on essentials like clothing basics (+210%) and hygiene products (+150%) alongside traditional gifts, driven by economic pressure; AI-driven traffic to retail sites is expected to grow 130% year over year.

title: Best Buy to launch on TikTok Shop
gist: Best Buy is launching on TikTok Shop in late October with nearly 10,000 products, fulfilled by Best Buy and returnable in-store, as it pursues a broader transformation into a retail media and technology company.

title: Target cuts prices as consumer sentiment sours
gist: Target is cutting prices on roughly 2,000 home, apparel and accessories items as consumer sentiment hits a four-month low, part of a broader 10,000-price-cut push over the past year.

title: Inflation slams consumer sentiment to 4-month low
gist: University of Michigan consumer sentiment dropped to a four-month low in September amid inflation and trade dispute concerns, yet retail sales jumped 1.2% in August, with e-commerce among the strongest-performing segments.

title: Brands Briefing: Hanna Andersson is joining Amazon, with a 90% unique assortment
gist: Hanna Andersson is launching an Amazon storefront on October 1, with 90% of its Amazon assortment being unique to the platform, drawn from archival best-sellers in matching sets, underwear and pajamas.

title: Beauty brand Cakes wants to turn its TikTok virality into an owned media strategy
gist: Cakes Body, a TikTok-viral beauty brand that hit $100M in sales in three years through founder-led storytelling, launched its own entertainment company called Cakes Media to systematize virality and improve profitability.

title: Sephora furthers UK ambitions via M&S shop-in-shops
gist: Sephora is partnering with Marks & Spencer to open shop-in-shop beauty spaces in 100 M&S UK stores and on M&S's website starting next spring, extending Sephora's UK footprint beyond its standalone locations.

title: Industry criticizes national parcel levy in Austria
gist: Austria has introduced a €2-per-parcel levy on online sellers and marketplaces with over €100M in annual Austrian sales, with industry groups strongly opposing the measure as it also affects thousands of smaller businesses indirectly.

title: AI Shopping Could Mean Fewer Returns
gist: Adobe Analytics data from over 1 trillion U.S. retail site visits shows AI-referred shoppers convert 60% more and generate 53% more revenue per visit, while 69% of AI-assisted shoppers report being less likely to return their purchases.

title: An Interview with Jason Del Rey About Muse, Amazon, and Walmart
gist: Stratechery's interview with Jason Del Rey covers Amazon vs. Meta's Muse and how it fits into the broader Amazon-Walmart rivalry, but the full content is behind a paywall.

title: Retailers pay 72p in tax for every £1 of profit as tax bill hits £62bn
gist: UK retailers pay 72p in tax for every £1 of pre-tax profit, contributing to a combined £62bn tax bill for retail and hospitality in 2025/26, with retail employment falling 122,000 jobs over two years as a result of rising cost burdens.

title: Two thirds of retailers plan store expansions despite economic uncertainty
gist: A CBRE survey of 76 pan-European retailers finds 65% plan to expand their store estates despite economic uncertainty, with over 90% expecting physical locations to remain core to their business and AI adoption in retail having doubled since 2024.

title: Weston family closes in on £7bn Boots takeover
gist: The Weston family behind Primark is reportedly close to acquiring Boots from Sycamore Partners for approximately £6.7bn, which would end speculation about a London IPO and add one of Britain's largest pharmacy chains to the family's retail portfolio.

title: Amazon wants to own the long game in ad measurement
gist: Amazon claims roughly 20% of a brand's sales value falls outside the standard 7–30 day attribution window, based on a study of over 2 million campaigns, and is now pushing for year-long measurement as competition from TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube intensifies.

title: OpenAI’s measurement gaps are keeping ChatGPT ads budgets at test level
gist: Seven months into selling ads on ChatGPT, OpenAI still lacks the measurement infrastructure marketers expect: agencies report conversion tracking failures, click-count discrepancies, delayed reporting, and no demographic or prompt-level data.

title: Media Briefing: Publishers are turning GEO from an experiment into a business
gist: Publishers are moving generative engine optimization (GEO) from experimental to a standard revenue line, with AI visibility in tools like ChatGPT and Google's AI Mode becoming a regular part of branded content deals.

title: In Graphic Detail: Where brands stand when AI agents do the shopping
gist: Analysis across ChatGPT, Google AI Mode, and Alexa for Shopping shows that AI shopping assistants produce radically different brand and retailer recommendations depending on which assistant is used, with Alexa heavily favoring Amazon's own store and ChatGPT spreading recommendations across 24 retailers.

title: ‘It scared the hell out of me to hand over the keys’: What brands have learned from creator partnerships
gist: Major retailers including Target, Gap, Aerie, and Kohl's are scaling creator programs in 2025–26, with nearly half of brands reporting 3x or greater ROI and creator budgets up 33% year over year, pointing to $13.7B in projected U.S. influencer spend by 2027.

title: DoorDash adds new retailers, texting shopping assistant
gist: DoorDash added Macy's, Anthropologie, The North Face, Vans, and Timberland to its retail marketplace and launched Dasher Returns (Dashers picking up return items) alongside Text DoorDash, an AI-powered conversational ordering assistant via SMS.

title: DoorDash launches an AI agent you can text to order food
gist: DoorDash launched an AI agent accessible via Apple Messages that lets users place food and retail orders through natural-language text prompts, handling group orders, dietary preferences, and recommendations without requiring the app.

title: ChatGPT can now virtually try on clothes for you
gist: OpenAI launched virtual try-on and a Favorites feature for ChatGPT globally, letting users upload photos to visualize clothing on themselves and save products for later. The features compete with Google and Pinterest in fashion discovery and could redirect shopping traffic away from traditional retail and search surfaces.

title: Big-Box Briefing: What to watch for as Amazon, Target and Walmart host their fall sales
gist: Amazon, Target, and Walmart are all running major fall sales events in the first week of October — Prime Big Deal Days, Walmart's Fall Deals Sale, and Target Circle Sale — serving as a key consumer demand signal ahead of the holiday season. This October sales cluster has grown into a significant retail period since Amazon introduced a second Prime Day in 2022.

title: Consumer confidence sags to 12-year low, eroded by inflation, job anxiety
gist: Consumer confidence dropped to a 12-year low, driven by fuel prices, high borrowing costs, and weak hiring, with median inflation expectations rising to 5.1% over the next 12 months. Economists note consumers feel more financially stressed now than during the 2020 pandemic.

title: The AI-powered holiday shopper: How prompt-driven curations and Gen Alpha algorithms will shape consumer behavior
gist: PwC's 2026 Holiday Outlook highlights AI-driven gift curation, AI price tracking, and Gen Alpha's growing algorithmic influence on household spending as major forces shaping this holiday shopping season. Gen Z is also showing record in-store foot traffic alongside digital AI-assisted behaviors.

title: Shopify debuts Canvas, a way to build online stores by chatting with AI
gist: Shopify launched Canvas, a conversational AI site-builder that lets merchants design and build their entire store by chatting with the Sidekick AI agent, with changes rendered in real-time against the actual store code. Initial limitations include no third-party theme support, no app blocks, and desktop-only access.

title: Consumer AI use a boon for the holidays as AI traffic doubles
gist: Adobe forecasts AI-referred traffic to U.S. retail sites will more than double this holiday season (+130% YoY), and consumers arriving via AI assistants add items to carts at a 32% higher rate and generate 43% more revenue per visit compared to non-AI traffic. Adobe also found that shoppers using AI feel more confident in purchases and are less likely to return items.

title: Holiday hiring is getting ‘smaller and more surgical’
gist: Seasonal retail hiring in the U.S. is expected to fall 2.5% year-over-year to ~450,000 new Q4 jobs, continuing a multi-year trend toward smaller, more surgical staffing rather than large seasonal waves. Retailers are leaning on existing staff and on-demand pools, with major names like Amazon, Target, and Bath & Body Works yet to announce 2026 hiring plans.

title: AI Shopping Upends the Rules of Brand Leadership, Price Positioning & Competition, According to New Jellyfish Research
gist: Jellyfish research found that AI shopping assistants (ChatGPT, Google AI Mode, Amazon Alexa) produce radically different product recommendations for identical queries, with no dominant 'AI shelf,' collapsed price tiers, and brand leadership often erased — ChatGPT alone accounted for ~80% of AI product recommendations across categories studied. The firm launched a 'Share of Model Shopping Optimization' tool to help brands measure and influence AI-level product visibility at the SKU level.

title: Meta debuts AI agent for small businesses
gist: Meta launched Muse for Small Business, an AI agent that integrates with Shopify, Stripe, QuickBooks, and other platforms to perform tasks on behalf of small businesses, priced at $20–$100/month after a free tier. Amazon has already asked Meta to remove its site from Muse's access, mirroring a prior legal dispute with Perplexity over unauthorized AI-agent purchases.

title: Nike plots further job cuts as China sales plunge 26%
gist: Nike reported a 4% revenue decline in Q1 to $11.21bn, with Greater China sales plunging 26% for the ninth consecutive quarter of decline, prompting restructuring plans and further job cuts expected to save ~£1.9bn by 2031. The company is simplifying its global structure from four regions to three and cutting Jordan retro launches to reduce discounting.

title: How Litter Robot is doing TikTok Shop without the deep discounts
gist: Whisker (maker of Litter Robot) joined TikTok Shop in the past year to capture early-mover advantage and reach Gen Z/Gen Alpha, without relying on the heavy discounting common on the platform.

title: Over 90% of purchases abroad made on Temu, Shein or AliExpress
gist: In 2025, over 90% of EU cross-border online spending on physical goods went to Temu, Shein, and AliExpress, totaling €49.7 billion out of €55.1 billion spent outside the EU.

title: Ikea to shutter 3 small-format plan and order stores
gist: IKEA U.S. is closing three small-format plan-and-order stores in the D.C. area, pivoting investment toward home delivery, pickup services, and digital channels instead.

title: Nike extends turnaround timeline amid more layoffs, sales declines
gist: Nike reported Q1 revenue down 4% to $11.2 billion and announced a third restructuring plan called 'Pace,' with more layoffs ahead and executives warning the turnaround will extend well beyond fiscal 2026.

title: What Meta got right with Muse
gist: Meta's Muse project is discussed on Hacker News, but no article text is available beyond the link.

title: 5 Content Marketing Ideas for November 2026
gist: Practical Ecommerce outlines five content marketing angles for November 2026, including Route 66's centennial, STEM Day product explainers, a 1976 retrospective, World Television Day tie-ins, and an 'anti-gift guide' format aimed at standing out in AI-assisted search.

title: We're going to need default hard budget caps on pretty much everything
gist: The post argues that pay-per-use APIs and cloud services should default to hard spending caps that cut off service at a set dollar limit, rather than soft warnings, noting AWS and Google Cloud have recently launched early versions of this feature.

title: All the AI agents that can live in your text messages
gist: TechCrunch surveys over a dozen AI personal assistant products that operate via SMS/iMessage, capable of handling tasks like scheduling, shopping, reservations, and email management without requiring a separate app download.

title: Gap unveils AI-assisted shopping, three decades after its first website
gist: Gap Inc. is launching AI-powered shopping tools across all four of its brands, partnering with platforms Alta Daily and Daydream for outfit discovery, plus adding conversational shopping agents to Old Navy and Banana Republic sites — 30 years after launching its first e-commerce website. The company acknowledges consumer skepticism, with 45% of AI-assisted apparel purchases resulting in regret according to one survey.

title: TikTok Shop still much bigger in the UK than elsewhere in Europe
gist: TikTok Shop's UK gross merchandise value is projected to reach nearly €5 billion in 2025, far outpacing its performance in other European markets where the platform has also launched.

title: Walmart to build Ohio fulfillment center for oversized goods
gist: Walmart is investing $300 million in a new fulfillment center in Ohio dedicated to oversized, non-sortable goods like furniture and TVs, part of a broader network reshuffling that also includes robotics upgrades and some facility closures. Amazon and Costco are making similar moves in the big-and-bulky category.

title: TikTok’s ad network bet: More reach, more budget
gist: TikTok has rebranded its Pangle ad network as the TikTok Ad Network (TTAN) and opened it to U.S. advertisers, allowing them to extend campaigns across nearly 400,000 apps beyond TikTok itself. The move is designed to capture more of advertisers' total budgets, though transparency about which apps are included remains limited.

title: Pricing tactics come under scrutiny in the age of AI
gist: Retailers are facing growing consumer and regulatory scrutiny over dynamic pricing practices, fueled by the spread of digital shelf labels and leaked screenshots of pricing algorithms. The pressure is putting more companies on the defensive about how customer data is used to set prices.

title: How GLP-1 users are forcing retailers to rethink everything
gist: GLP-1 weight-loss drug adoption — now at 11% of U.S. adults — is driving measurable shifts in apparel retail: smaller average dress sizes, delayed purchases, higher return rates, and surge in bracketing behavior. Retailers like David's Bridal and DXL are adapting operations around sizing volatility, with 70% of GLP-1 users having dropped at least one clothing size.

title: Lidl attracts 43m extra visits as Lidl Plus investment fuels growth
gist: Lidl GB grew revenue 10.8% to £13bn, driven partly by a 23% rise in Lidl Plus loyalty app users, with more than half of shoppers now using a loyalty coupon vs. a quarter the prior year. The retailer plans a 60% increase in personalized coupon funding in 2026 alongside continued physical expansion.

title: OpenAI moves to make ChatGPT ads more measurable — and more visual
gist: OpenAI is expanding ChatGPT's ad product with new image ad formats and improved measurement tools, addressing advertiser complaints about limited formats and inability to track performance since ads launched in February. Tests of image ads in the U.S. are planned for later this month.

title: From influencers to AI, here’s what Gen Alpha thinks about your brand
gist: A panel of Gen Alpha shoppers at Shoptalk Fall revealed strong aversion to AI-generated ads and a preference for feeling 'unique,' with the cohort holding $100 billion in direct annual spending power and influencing nearly half of U.S. household spend in families with children ages 8–14. Amazon, Nike, and McDonald's are currently the top-ranked brands among Gen Alpha teens.

title: TikTok rolls out an AI shopping assistant and one-click checkout
gist: TikTok is launching a conversational AI shopping assistant and a one-click checkout directly in the For You feed, built with partners including Shopify, Salesforce, and Stripe, expanding its commerce push beyond TikTok Shop.

title: Shapermint is on track to hit $10M in TikTok Shop sales by targeting women ages 35-65
gist: Shaperwear brand Shapermint built a 5,000-creator affiliate network on TikTok Shop — 60% of its top creators are over 35 — driving 515% month-over-month growth and putting it on track for $10M in TikTok Shop sales this year.

title: ASOS app users receive push notifications apparently sent by hackers
gist: ASOS users received push notifications apparently sent by hackers claiming to have compromised the retailer's Snowflake data instance, with the extortion message sent publicly through the app's own notification system.

title: OpenAI launches visual ads that appear alongside image generation results
gist: OpenAI is adding visual display ads to ChatGPT that appear alongside image generation results, with measurement partnerships including AppsFlyer, Triple Whale, and Northbeam among others, initially rolling out in the U.S.

title: What the Super El Niño means for retail
gist: A record-strength El Niño is expected to produce an unusually warm fall and winter in North America, putting pressure on seasonal inventory and margins for apparel and winter-gear retailers, while a cold snap is forecast for early next year.

title: Amazon holds 63% of German online retail
gist: Amazon holds a 63% share of Germany's online retail market, with nearly all German online shoppers using the platform, and the company directly or indirectly influencing 41% of German spending in studied product categories.

title: Retail media hits £2bn as UK ad spend jumps 32% in H1
gist: UK retail media advertising grew 32% year-on-year in H1 2026 to reach £2bn, making it the fastest-growing digital ad category and placing it ahead of gaming, digital out-of-home, and classified advertising.

title: ‘Defensible to the CFO’: Prime Day catalyzes Amazon video and DSP spend growth
gist: Media buyers report Amazon Ads spend ahead of Prime Big Deal Days is up 15–40% year-on-year, with full-year growth projected at up to 33%, driven by both endemic and non-endemic advertisers.

title: How to find out if Amazon thinks you have ‘flat buttocks’
gist: Amazon's 'Shopping Preferences' section reveals detailed inferences about customers based on purchase history, including physical and lifestyle characteristics, as highlighted by a viral Threads post showing an assumption about a shopper's body type.

title: ASOS admits that “basic personal information” may have been accessed in cyberattack
gist: ASOS confirmed that 'basic personal information' may have been accessed in a cyberattack after hackers sent an unauthorized pop-up to customers claiming to have compromised its Snowflake data storage instance; the company said payment card data and passwords are not believed to have been accessed.

title: The next hurdle for AI agents: getting websites to let them in
gist: Personal AI agents like Meta's Muse are being blocked by major retailers and websites — sometimes intentionally, sometimes accidentally — as existing anti-bot infrastructure cannot distinguish between malicious bots and AI agents acting on behalf of users, prompting an industry push for a new open standard for agent-to-commerce communication.

title: Walmart defends pricing practices, again
gist: Walmart is publicly denying it uses or plans to use digital shelf labels for dynamic or personalized pricing, while advocacy group Groundwork Collaborative points to granted patents describing such capabilities and argues the retailer's public and investor communications are inconsistent.

title: Hackers target ASOS with unusual pop-up extortion attempt
gist: ASOS was targeted by hackers who sent an unauthorized pop-up extortion message to customers via its mobile app, claiming to have compromised its Snowflake cloud database instance and threatening to leak data unless ASOS engaged with them; shares fell 5% within minutes.

title: Brands Briefing: Why Crocs, David’s Bridal and StockX are embracing episodic content
gist: Brands including Crocs, David's Bridal, and StockX are increasing investment in episodic short-form content as a marketing channel, following examples from Dr. Pepper, Marc Jacobs, and Bob's Discount Furniture, which have produced original series to engage audiences.

title: AI shopping has outrun its plumbing, says payments expert
gist: AI shopping agents like Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots can now execute purchases on consumers' behalf via integrated payment rails, but a payments expert warns the commercial framework — fraud standards, agent identity verification, dispute resolution — is not yet in place to support this at scale.

title: Desktop Habits Hide Mobile Friction
gist: A practical audit checklist for mobile e-commerce UX, covering pop-up sequencing, sticky header conflicts, in-app browser limitations, and touch-optimized interactions — all issues that arise because store operators typically review their sites on desktop rather than mobile.

title: Fashion Briefing: How 3 fashion brands crossed $100 million in revenue without outside investment
gist: Glossy interviewed three fashion brand founders who scaled past $100M in revenue without outside investment, framing self-funded growth as an increasingly critical skill as VC dollars dry up — full article behind a paywall.

title: Lululemon’s Heidi O’Neill overhauls C-suite in first move as CEO
gist: New Lululemon CEO Heidi O'Neill has restructured the C-suite one month into the role, creating chief product and chief operating officer positions and removing two existing executives, with the stated aim of putting product design and innovation at the company's operational center.

title: How agentic commerce helps brands like Willy Chavarria optimize for BFCM
gist: E-commerce brands are turning to agentic commerce tools — AI-powered storefronts and checkout experiences — to improve conversion during BFCM, with the argument that speed of answer, not depth of discount, determines who wins peak season.

title: Swedish ecommerce grew 8% in Q2
gist: Swedish e-commerce grew 8% year-over-year in Q2, with all online sectors contributing to the increase. Whether the trend holds through the rest of the year remains to be seen.

title: Future of Marketing Briefing: Why top creators are taking fewer brand deals
gist: Top creators are reducing the number of brand deals they take and demanding more from the partners they keep — including equity stakes, product input, and formal titles. The shift was a recurring theme at Advertising Week New York.

title: Why ChatGPT ads won’t likely impact holiday sales in a major way this year
gist: Brands testing ChatGPT's ad platform don't expect it to materially move holiday sales, citing high cost-per-click rates, unproven conversion, and lack of trust as a product-recommendation source. Most advertisers still treat it as an experimental channel versus Meta or Google.

title: Pop Newsletter: College-age creators are embracing Amazon and ShopMy, moving away from Shein and malls
gist: College-age creators at a Glossy roundtable report gravitating toward Amazon and ShopMy for affiliate revenue while moving away from Shein and mall-based shopping. Platform usability and payout reliability appear to be key deciding factors.

title: Big-Box Briefing: Why executive turnover has been a consistent theme in retail media
gist: The departure of Albertsons Media Collective's head Brian Monahan highlights ongoing executive instability in retail media leadership. The pattern of turnover points to structural challenges facing retail media networks.

title: Wholesale, tariff refunds deliver for Levi’s in rough Q3
gist: Levi's Q3 net revenues rose 4% to $1.6B, but DTC growth was nearly flat while wholesale grew 6%; tariff refunds of ~$80M boosted gross margins and are being reinvested into marketing and supply chain ahead of Q4. A mismatch between the brand's fit emphasis and consumer demand also weighed on results.

title: Amazon retail division hit by job cuts
gist: Amazon is cutting an undisclosed number of roles in its retail stores division, framing it as a structural adjustment to better execute on priorities. The cuts follow broader corporate layoffs announced in 2025, even as online store sales grew 15% year-over-year in Q2.

title: AI is ‘reshaping’ Walmart and Sparky is leading the charge
gist: Walmart's US CEO credits AI — particularly its in-house assistant Sparky and integrations with ChatGPT and Gemini — with driving a 10th consecutive quarter of 20%+ e-commerce growth, 40% higher AOVs from Sparky, and strong conversion from third-party AI agent referrals. Walmart is notably open to external AI agents, in contrast to Amazon's blocking approach.

title: Walmart debuts 1-hour express pickup, ASL service ahead of holidays
gist: Walmart is rolling out 1-hour express curbside pickup at 500 stores ahead of the holidays, alongside an in-store LED shelf-locator feature and American Sign Language interpreting at service desks. About 80% of Walmart's e-commerce deliveries already flow through stores.

title: Tesco doubles down on digital as profits and guidance climb
gist: Tesco raised its full-year profit guidance after H1 results showed 2% sales growth and 6.3% profit growth, with online sales up 8% and its rapid-delivery service Whoosh up 37%. The CEO pointed to AI-enabled personalization, retail media growth, and new delivery partnerships as key drivers.

title: AI will move at the speed of customer trust, not technology, says E.ON Next
gist: E.ON Next's digital AI lead argues that AI adoption by customers will be uneven and trust-dependent, not driven by technical capability, and that businesses should treat AI as a channel and product strategy rather than a one-off transformation project. He recommends funding outcomes — like sales or retention — rather than isolated AI features like chatbots.

title: Your Next Product Could Be a New Brand
gist: Agency founder Rok Hladnik advises DTC merchants to consider launching a separate brand rather than extending an existing one when targeting new audiences, and warns against cutting product quality as a red flag for long-term brand health. He also notes that AI is pressuring traditional media-buying agencies by enabling ad platforms to disintermediate them.
